headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: both agents can write files and run shells, with ECC also modifying git and using MCP, while Dify shares state via datastore.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible injection path exists because Dify can read uploaded knowledge-base files and write files, while ECC treats files, skills, hooks, and MCP configs as workflow surfaces. If Dify-produced content is later consumed by ECC, attacker-controlled text could steer actions. The shared channel is indirect, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Dify outputs are copied into ECC skills, hooks, or MCP configs
IF either agent parses file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Dify-generated files into ECC workflows
Add a manual review step before importing any shared file
Restrict ECC to read-only access for imported artifacts
Tag imported content as untrusted in operator notes
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets, while ECC touches session summaries, learned skills, git history, and security findings. Because both can read and write files and Dify shares state via a datastore, sensitive material can cross from one agent’s workspace into the other’s outputs in default multi-agent setups.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or datastore
IF conversation logs, security findings, or knowledge-base files are accessible to both agents
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different directories
Remove sensitive files from any shared workspace
Limit ECC access to non-sensitive subfolders
Review logs for accidental cross-agent copying
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and shell execution; ECC additionally has modify_git_state and use_mcp, while Dify has shared_state_with_other_instances via the Dify datastore. That creates a default conflict surface for concurrent edits and state corruption, especially around git or shared files, with no locking mechanism stated.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF ECC modifies git state while Dify writes files in the same tree
mitigations: Run the agents in separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files
Avoid git operations from ECC on shared repos
Check for file conflicts before each write
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC exposes a workflow surface with skills, hooks, and MCP configs, so it can plausibly act on Dify output. Dify can generate agent/workflow content and access knowledge-base material; if ECC treats that output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated facts can cascade into downstream actions or commits. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier.
conditions: IF Dify output is fed directly into ECC skills, hooks, or git changes
IF ECC executes or commits based on unverified Dify-generated text
mitigations: Require human review before ECC acts on Dify output
Mark Dify output as advisory only
Disable auto-commit paths in ECC for shared tasks
Compare Dify claims against source files before use
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches conversation logs and knowledge-base content, while ECC touches session summaries, metrics, git history, and security findings with retention-related secrets. The profiles show different data classes and retention surfaces, but no explicit residency or certification mismatch; the safest reading is a medium compliance gap from mixed logging and retention behavior.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in both agents' logs or summaries
IF retention settings differ between Dify datastore and ECC session storage
mitigations: Align retention settings before use
Exclude regulated data from session summaries
Document which data class each agent may store
Purge stale logs on a fixed schedule
requires-engineering: harmonize residency and retention controls
